what: Registration of the ceiling-field fix (Phase 20 Step 2), committed before any code change
defect: breakpoint_evidence_summary normalises evidence_score over the layers it counts (applicable_layers minus unassessable_layers), but the ceiling fields server.py's _with_ceiling adds (attainable_here, max_with_flat_depth, strong_band_reachable_here, attainable_basis, attainable_note) come from score_tiers.ceiling_from_observed, which always assumes all four layers are counted. Measured in before.json: at IMP01 chr20:200000 (default window) the score is 65.0 with [discordant_pairs, soft_clipped_reads] and 65.0 with [soft_clipped_reads, split_reads], while attainable_here reads 57.5 for every layer list; in the Phase 10 run files 5 of 72 summary calls passed a restricted list and 1 (qwen3.5:4b WITH run 15) returned a score above the reported ceiling.

rule.counted_layers: the return's applicable_layers minus its unassessable_layers, in that order -- exactly the layers in evidence_score's denominator
rule.attainable_here: round(100 x S / M, 1), where S sums over the counted layers: the discordant layer's observed tier score, the soft-clip and split-read maxima, and 0 for depth; and M is the sum of the counted layers' maxima. Rounded as evidence_score is. None when the discordant layer is counted and its observed value is missing, or when no layer is counted
rule.max_with_flat_depth: round(100 x (sum of the counted layers' maxima except depth) / M, 1)
rule.max_all_layers: unchanged (100: every counted layer at its maximum normalises to 100)
rule.new_field: ceiling_counted_layers names the counted layers; it is added only when fewer than four layers are counted, so that the default return, and the model-visible payload built from it, stay byte-identical
rule.sentences: when fewer than four layers are counted, attainable_basis and attainable_note say which ones and describe only those
rule.single_derivation: score_tiers.ceiling_from_observed takes the counted layers; server.py's _with_ceiling and ui.py's evidence panel both pass them

default_identity: with no layer list, or with all four layers counted (in any order), every ceiling field must be byte-identical to today's
authorised_files: stage1_igv_assistant/server.py (_with_ceiling; one docstring sentence if it describes the ceiling)
no_changes_to: any threshold, tier, band, window or default
tests: stage1_igv_assistant/tests/test_ceiling_layers.py, written first and shown failing on the pre-fix score_tiers.py and server.py (loaded from git into scratch modules). Self-contained: tiers derived from the source, synthetic observed values, no BAM; plus one integration check through the MCP dispatch at IMP01. Positive control: with a restricted list the ceiling equals the normalised maximum over those layers, and whenever the depth component is 0 the score does not exceed attainable_here. Negative control: with all four layers and with no list, every ceiling field equals the pre-fix output.
remeasurement: after.json and suites.json: (a) the four IMP01 calls, score and ceiling agreeing and matching the expected values above; (b) the 40 implant and 54 background breakends, default geometry, all four layers: every ceiling field byte-identical to before.json; (c) the prepared-payload proof re-run, its locus's model-visible payload byte-identical to the 2026-09-26 proof; (d) ui --check exit 0 and the IMP01 panel still 40.0 and 57.5; (e) every suite in stage1_igv_assistant/tests/ with the assertion census (scripts/run_suites.py).
guard: after the fix is committed, scripts/guard_protected.py's DEFAULT_BASE moves to the fix commit
